hindi: अब इसके बाद हम 'अपामार्गतण्डुलीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called "Apāmārgataṇḍulīya".
notes: Prose opening formula, not a verse (the unit is typed as "verse"). The title is a taddhita name from the chapter's opening words (apāmārgasya bījāni, 'seeds of apāmārga'; taṇḍula = grain, seed).

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, not a verse. sma with āha gives a past sense.

hindi: अपामार्ग के बीज, पिप्पली और मरिच, फिर विडङ्ग, शिग्रु, सर्षप और तुम्बुरु,
english: The seeds of apāmārga, pippalī and marica, then viḍaṅga, śigru, sarṣapa and tumburu,
notes: A list in the accusative, the object of dadyāt in 5b (the sentence runs 3a to 5b). The plural forms (maricāni, viḍaṅgāni, śigrūṇi, tumburūṇi) refer to the seeds or fruits. Identifications: apāmārga = Achyranthes aspera, Hindi चिरचिटा (standard); pippalī = Piper longum, long pepper, Hindi पीपल (standard); marica = Piper nigrum, black pepper, Hindi काली मिर्च (standard); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes, Hindi वायविडंग (standard); śigru = Moringa oleifera, Hindi सहजन (standard); sarṣapa = mustard, Brassica species, Hindi सरसों (standard); tumburu = a Zanthoxylum species, Hindi तेजबल (probable).

hindi: अजाजी और अजगन्धा, पीलु, एला, हरेणुका, पृथ्वीका, सुरसा, श्वेता, कुठेरक और फणिज्झक,
english: ajājī and ajagandhā, pīlu, elā, hareṇukā, pṛthvīkā, surasā, śvetā, kuṭheraka and phaṇijjhaka,
notes: Continues the accusative list of 3. Identifications: ajājī = cumin, Cuminum cyminum, Hindi जीरा (probable; some take black cumin); ajagandhā = Cleome gynandra, Hindi हुलहुल (probable); pīlu = Salvadora persica, Hindi पीलू (standard); elā = small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum, Hindi इलायची (standard); hareṇukā = seeds of Vitex agnus-castus, Hindi रेणुका (probable); pṛthvīkā = disputed (large cardamom or Nigella sativa, Hindi कलौंजी, proposed); surasā = holy basil, Ocimum tenuiflorum, Hindi तुलसी (standard); śvetā = disputed (often taken as a white variety of surasā; other plants proposed); kuṭheraka = an Ocimum species (probable); phaṇijjhaka = an Ocimum or marjoram-like plant, Hindi मरुवा (probable).

hindi: शिरीष के बीज, लशुन, दोनों हरिद्रा, दो लवण, ज्योतिष्मती और नागर को शीर्षविरेचन में देना चाहिए।
english: the seed of śirīṣa, laśuna, the two haridrās, the two salts, jyotiṣmatī and nāgara one should give in head-evacuation (śīrṣavirecana).
notes: dadyāt governs the whole list from 3a. haridre (dual): commentators take it as haridrā and dāruharidrā; lavaṇadvaya (two salts): commentators take it as saindhava and sauvarcala; the text names neither pair. śīrṣavirecana = śirovirecana. Identifications: śirīṣa = Albizia lebbeck, Hindi सिरस (standard); laśuna = garlic, Allium sativum, Hindi लहसुन (standard); haridrā = Curcuma longa, Hindi हल्दी (standard); dāruharidrā = Berberis aristata, Hindi दारुहल्दी (standard); jyotiṣmatī = Celastrus paniculatus, Hindi मालकांगनी (standard); nāgara = dry ginger, Zingiber officinale, Hindi सोंठ (standard).

hindi: सिर के भारीपन में, शूल में, पीनस में, अर्धावभेदक में, कृमि रोग में, अपस्मार में, घ्राणनाश में और प्रमोहक में।
english: In heaviness of the head, in pain, in pīnasa, in ardhāvabhedaka (one-sided splitting headache), in worm disease, in apasmāra, in loss of smell and in pramohaka.
notes: The indications for the head-evacuation of 5b. śirasaḥ may govern śūle as well ("heaviness and pain of the head"). Usual modern equivalents: pīnasa = chronic rhinitis, coryza (standard); ardhāvabhedaka = hemicrania, migraine-like one-sided headache (standard); apasmāra = epilepsy (standard); pramohaka = stupor or fainting (probable). krimi is the usual variant spelling of kṛmi.

hindi: मदन, मधुक, निम्ब, जीमूत, कृतवेधन, पिप्पली, कुटज, इक्ष्वाकु, एला और धामार्गव,
english: Madana, madhuka, nimba, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana, pippalī, kuṭaja, ikṣvāku, elā and dhāmārgava,
notes: Accusative list, the object of prayuñjīta in 8b. Identifications: madana = Catunaregam spinosa (Randia dumetorum), Hindi मैनफल (standard); madhuka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, Hindi मुलेठी (standard; some take Madhuca species); nimba = Azadirachta indica, Hindi नीम (standard); jīmūta = Luffa echinata, Hindi देवदाली (probable); kṛtavedhana = bitter Luffa acutangula, Hindi कड़वी तोरई (probable); kuṭaja = Holarrhena pubescens, Hindi कुड़ा (standard); ikṣvāku = bitter Lagenaria siceraria, Hindi कड़वी तुम्बी (standard); elā = small cardamom (standard); dhāmārgava = a Luffa species (probable).

words.gram: pres. part. caus. m. nom. sg. a-√duṣ

hindi: श्लेष्मा और पित्त के उपस्थित होने पर, आमाशय में स्थित रोग में, भिषक् शरीर को दूषित न करते हुए वमन के लिए प्रयोग करे।
english: When Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta have come up, in a disease seated in the āmāśaya, the physician, not harming the body, should employ for emesis (vamana).
notes: The object of prayuñjīta is the list of 7. upasthite śleṣmapitte is a locative absolute; upasthita is read as "risen, ready for elimination" by commentators. āmāśaya, literally "seat of unripe matter", is usually rendered stomach (standard).

hindi: त्रिवृत्, त्रिफला, दन्ती, नीलिनी, सप्तला, वचा, कम्पिल्लक, गवाक्षी, क्षीरिणी और उदकीर्यका,
english: Trivṛt, triphalā, dantī, nīlinī, saptalā, vacā, kampillaka, gavākṣī, kṣīriṇī and udakīryakā,
notes: Accusative list, the object of prayojayet in 10b. trivṛtām is from the ā-stem trivṛtā, a variant of trivṛt. Identifications: trivṛt = Operculina turpethum, Hindi निशोथ (standard); triphalā = harītakī, vibhītaka and āmalakī together (standard); dantī = Baliospermum montanum, Hindi दन्ती (standard); nīlinī = indigo, Indigofera tinctoria, Hindi नील (standard); saptalā = disputed (an Acacia or Euphorbia species proposed); vacā = Acorus calamus, Hindi वच (standard); kampillaka = Mallotus philippensis, Hindi कमीला (standard); gavākṣī = disputed (a colocynth-like cucurbit proposed); kṣīriṇī = disputed (a latex-bearing plant); udakīryakā = udakīryā, disputed (a karañja-type tree, Pongamia, proposed).

hindi: पीलु, आरग्वध, द्राक्षा, द्रवन्ती और निचुल को, दोष के पक्वाशय में चले जाने पर, विरेचन के लिए प्रयोग करे।
english: pīlu, āragvadha, drākṣā, dravantī and nicula one should use for purgation (vireka) when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya.
notes: The sentence runs from 9a. vireka = virecana. pakvāśaya, literally "seat of digested matter", is usually rendered large intestine (standard). Identifications: āragvadha = Cassia fistula, Hindi अमलतास (standard); drākṣā = grape, Vitis vinifera, Hindi दाख (standard); dravantī = disputed (a dantī-like plant, Croton or Jatropha species proposed); nicula = Barringtonia acutangula, Hindi हिज्जल (probable); pīlu = Salvadora persica (standard).

hindi: पाटला और अग्निमन्थ, बिल्व और श्योनाक भी, काश्मर्य, शालपर्णी, पृश्निपर्णी और निदिग्धिका,
english: Pāṭalā and agnimantha, bilva and also śyonāka, kāśmarya, śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī and nidigdhikā,
notes: Accusative list running to 13a, the object of yuñjyāt in 13b. With bṛhatī and śvadaṃṣṭrā of 12a these make up the group later called daśamūla (ten roots); the text here does not name the group. Identifications: pāṭalā = Stereospermum suaveolens, Hindi पाढ़ल (standard); agnimantha = Premna serratifolia (P. integrifolia), Hindi अरणी (standard); bilva = Aegle marmelos, Hindi बेल (standard); śyonāka = Oroxylum indicum, Hindi सोनापाठा (standard); kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea, Hindi गम्भारी (standard); śālaparṇī = Desmodium gangeticum, Hindi सरिवन (standard); pṛśniparṇī = Uraria picta, Hindi पिठवन (standard); nidigdhikā = kaṇṭakārī, Solanum virginianum, Hindi कटेरी (standard).

hindi: बला, श्वदंष्ट्रा, बृहती, पुनर्नवा सहित एरण्ड, यव, कुलत्थ, कोल, गुडूची और मदन,
english: balā, śvadaṃṣṭrā, bṛhatī, eraṇḍa together with punarnavā, yava, kulattha, kola, guḍūcī and madana,
notes: sapunarnavam agrees with eraṇḍam (or may be read as an adverbial "with punarnavā"). Identifications: balā = Sida cordifolia, Hindi खरैटी (standard); śvadaṃṣṭrā = gokṣura, Tribulus terrestris, Hindi गोखरू (standard); bṛhatī = Solanum indicum, Hindi बड़ी कटेरी (standard); eraṇḍa = castor, Ricinus communis, Hindi अरंडी (standard); punarnavā = Boerhavia diffusa, Hindi साँठ (standard); yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare, Hindi जौ (standard); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum, Hindi कुलथी (standard); kola = jujube, Ziziphus species, Hindi बेर (standard); guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia, Hindi गिलोय (standard); madana = Catunaregam spinosa (standard).

hindi: पलाश, कत्तृण, और स्नेह तथा लवण भी, उदावर्त में, विबन्धों में और आस्थापनों में प्रयोग करे।
english: palāśa, kattṛṇa, and also unctuous substances (sneha) and salts, one should use in udāvarta, in obstructions (vibandha) and in decoction enemas (āsthāpana).
notes: The list runs from 11a. The three locatives may also be read as "in decoction enemas, for udāvarta and obstructions". Usual modern equivalents: udāvarta = upward reversal of flatus, faeces and urine with retention (standard); vibandha = constipation, obstruction (standard). Identifications: palāśa = Butea monosperma, Hindi पलाश/ढाक (standard); kattṛṇa = rohiṣa grass, a Cymbopogon species (probable).

hindi: इसी औषधगण से मारुत को नष्ट करने वाले अनुवासन की कल्पना करनी चाहिए। इस प्रकार पञ्चकर्म से सम्बन्धित संग्रह कहा गया।
english: From this very group of medicines an unctuous enema (anuvāsana) that destroys Vāta (māruta) is to be devised. Thus the collection relating to the five procedures (pañcakarma) has been declared.
notes: ata ... gaṇāt: the group of 11a to 13a. mārutaghnam is read with anuvāsanam; it can also be read as "(drugs) destroying Vāta" chosen from the group. iti closes the five-procedure collection (head-evacuation, emesis, purgation, decoction enema, unctuous enema).

words.gloss: of those whose doṣas have come up
with preparation by oleation and sweating
words.gram: n. inst. pl. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
pres. part. caus. m. nom. sg. vi-√car

hindi: जिनके दोष उपस्थित हो गए हैं, उनके लिए स्नेह और स्वेद द्वारा तैयारी के साथ, मात्रा और काल का विचार करते हुए, उन पञ्चकर्मों को करे।
english: Those five procedures (pañcakarma) one should perform for persons whose doṣas have come up, with preparation by oleation and sweating (sneha, sveda), considering dose and time.
notes: upasthitadoṣāṇām is a genitive ("of those whose doṣas have come up"), rendered "for". upapādana may also mean "making fit": the patients are made fit by oleation and sweating.

hindi: युक्ति मात्रा और काल पर आश्रित है; सिद्धि युक्ति में प्रतिष्ठित है। युक्ति को जानने वाला द्रव्यों का ज्ञान रखने वालों से सदा ऊपर स्थित रहता है।
english: Rational planning (yukti) rests on dose and time; success is established in yukti. The knower of yukti always stands above those who have knowledge of substances (dravya).
notes: The comma after yuktiḥ is in the printed text. upari with the genitive: "above, superior to".

hindi: इसके आगे मैं, उनसे साध्य विविध विकारों की निवृत्ति के लिए, विविध औषधियों से युक्त यवागुओं को कहूँगा।
english: After this I shall declare gruels (yavāgū) with various medicines, for the cessation of various disorders curable by them.
notes: tatsādhya: "curable by them" (by the gruels) or "curable by that". yavāgū is a thin gruel of grain cooked in liquid.

words.gloss: with pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and nāgara

words.gram: ppp. f. nom. sg. caus. upa-√sādh

hindi: पिप्पली, पिप्पलीमूल, चव्य, चित्रक और नागर से बनाई गई यवागू दीपनीय और शूलनाशक होती है।
english: Gruel prepared with pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and nāgara stimulates digestion (dīpanīya) and destroys colic pain (śūla).
notes: First of the twenty-eight gruels counted in 34. Identifications: pippalīmūla = root of Piper longum, Hindi पीपलामूल (standard); cavya = Piper retrofractum (P. chaba), Hindi चव्य (standard); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica, Hindi चीता (standard); nāgara = dry ginger (standard).

words.gloss: prepared with dadhittha, bilva, cāṅgerī, buttermilk and dāḍima
words.gram: f. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: दधित्थ, बिल्व, चाङ्गेरी, तक्र और दाडिम से बनाई गई यवागू पाचनी और ग्राहिणी होती है; वात युक्त अवस्था में पञ्चमूल से बनी पेया।
english: Prepared with dadhittha, bilva, cāṅgerī, buttermilk (takra) and dāḍima, it is digesting (pācana) and binding (grāhin); when Vāta is involved, a peyā made with the five roots (pāñcamūlikī).
notes: Two gruels (the 2nd and 3rd of the 28). savāte: commentators read "in diarrhoea with Vāta", carrying atisāra from 20b; the text has only "with Vāta". Which pañcamūla (lesser or greater five roots) is meant is not stated; commentators differ. peyā is a thinner gruel than yavāgū. Identifications: dadhittha = kapittha, wood apple, Limonia acidissima, Hindi कैथ (standard); cāṅgerī = Oxalis corniculata, Hindi अमलोनी (standard); dāḍima = pomegranate, Punica granatum, Hindi अनार (standard).

words.gloss: for those with diarrhoea of Pitta and Kapha

hindi: शालपर्णी, बला और बिल्व से और पृश्निपर्णी से सिद्ध, दाडिम से अम्ल की गई पेया पित्त और श्लेष्मा के अतिसार वालों के लिए हितकर है।
english: Peyā prepared with śālaparṇī, balā and bilva and with pṛśniparṇī, soured with dāḍima, is beneficial for those with diarrhoea (atisāra) of Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman).
notes: vilva is a common spelling of bilva (v/b), not flagged. pittaśleṣmātisāra may mean diarrhoea of Pitta and of Kapha (two kinds) or of both together. Identifications: see 11 (śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bilva), 12 (balā), 19 (dāḍima).

hindi: आधा जल मिले बकरी के पय में ह्रीबेर, उत्पल और नागर से तथा पृश्निपर्णी से सिद्ध पेया रक्तातिसार को नष्ट करती है।
english: Peyā prepared in goat's milk with half water, with hrīvera, utpala and nāgara and with pṛśniparṇī, destroys bloody diarrhoea (raktātisāra).
notes: cchāge: the cch is regular sandhi after the vowel of ardhodake; the word is chāge. ardhodaka: milk mixed with half its quantity of water (commentators); the text says only "half water". Identifications: hrīvera = disputed (Pavonia odorata or Plectranthus vettiveroides, Hindi सुगंधबाला, proposed); utpala = blue water-lily, a Nymphaea species, Hindi नीलकमल (standard).

hindi: आम की अवस्था में अतिविषा सहित, अम्ल सहित और नागर सहित पेया देनी चाहिए; मूत्रकृच्छ्र में श्वदंष्ट्रा और कण्टकारी से, फाणित सहित।
english: When there is āma (undigested matter), one should give peyā with ativiṣā, soured and with nāgara; in painful urination (mūtrakṛcchra), with śvadaṃṣṭrā and kaṇṭakārī, with phāṇita.
notes: Two gruels. sāme: commentators read "in diarrhoea with āma" (āmātisāra); the text has only "with āma". The sour ingredient of sāmlām is not named. phāṇita = cane juice boiled down to a thick syrup. Identifications: ativiṣā = Aconitum heterophyllum, Hindi अतीस (standard); kaṇṭakārī = Solanum virginianum, Hindi कटेरी (standard); śvadaṃṣṭrā = gokṣura (standard).

hindi: विडङ्ग, पिप्पलीमूल और शिग्रु से तथा मरिच से, तक्र में सिद्ध, सुवर्चिका सहित यवागू कृमिनाशक होती है।
english: Gruel cooked in buttermilk (takra) with viḍaṅga, pippalīmūla and śigru and with marica, with suvarcikā, destroys worms (krimi).
notes: suvarcikā: disputed (sauvarcala salt, or svarjikā alkali, natron, proposed by commentators). Plants: see 3 and 18.

words.gloss: with mṛdvīkā, sārivā, parched grain, pippalī, honey and nāgara

hindi: मृद्वीका, सारिवा, लाजा, पिप्पली, मधु और नागर से यह पिपासा को नष्ट करती है; और सोमराजी से पकाई गई यह विष को नष्ट करती है।
english: With mṛdvīkā, sārivā, lāja (parched grain), pippalī, honey (madhu) and nāgara it destroys thirst; and cooked with somarājī it destroys poison.
notes: Two gruels. Line a has no participle; "prepared" is understood from the series. The comma after pipāsāghnī is printed. Identifications: mṛdvīkā = grape, raisin (standard); sārivā = Hemidesmus indicus, Hindi अनन्तमूल (standard); somarājī = bākucī, Cullen corylifolium (Psoralea corylifolia), Hindi बावची (standard).

hindi: वराह के निर्यूह में सिद्ध यवागू बृंहणी मानी गई है; भुनी हुई गवेधुका की, माक्षिक सहित यवागू कर्शनीय है।
english: Gruel cooked in boar soup (varāha-niryūha) is considered nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa); that of roasted gavedhukā, with honey (mākṣika), is reducing (karśana).
notes: Two gruels. niryūha = extract, soup. Identification: gavedhukā = Job's tears, Coix lacryma-jobi (probable).

words.gloss: in the decoction of kuśa and āmalaka

hindi: घृत युक्त, अधिक तिल वाली और लवण युक्त यवागू स्नेहनी है; कुश और आमलक के निर्यूह में श्यामाक की यवागू विरूक्षणी है।
english: Containing ghee, with much sesame and with salt, it is oleating (snehana); that of śyāmāka in the decoction of kuśa and āmalaka is drying (virūkṣaṇa).

text_flags.why: The word is from vi-√rūkṣ with long ū (virūkṣaṇa); the Devanagari also has short उ (विरुक्षणी). The metre favours the long vowel (syllables 5-7 of the even pāda should be short-long-short). Probable typo.

notes: Two gruels. Identifications: kuśa = Desmostachya bipinnata, Hindi कुश (standard); āmalaka = Phyllanthus emblica, Hindi आँवला (standard); śyāmāka = Echinochloa frumentacea, Hindi साँवा (standard); tila = sesame (standard).

words.gloss: removing cough, hiccup, dyspnoea and Kapha

hindi: दशमूली से पकाई गई यवागू कास, हिक्का, श्वास और कफ को दूर करती है; यमक में मदिरा से सिद्ध यवागू पक्वाशय की पीड़ा को दूर करती है।
english: Boiled with the ten roots (daśamūlī), it removes cough (kāsa), hiccup, dyspnoea (śvāsa) and Kapha; cooked with madirā in yamaka, it removes pain of the pakvāśaya.
notes: Two gruels. daśamūlī: the ten roots of 11 and 12a (commentators). yamaka: commentators explain it as a pair of fats (ghee and oil) in which the gruel is fried; the text does not define it. madirā = a kind of liquor.

words.gloss: with stones of jambū and āmra, sour dadhittha and bilva

hindi: शाक, मांस, तिल और माष से सिद्ध यवागू वर्च को बाहर निकालती है; जम्बू और आम्र की गुठली, अम्ल दधित्थ और बिल्व से यह साङ्ग्राहिकी मानी गई है।
english: Cooked with vegetables (śāka), meats, sesame (tila) and māṣa, it expels faeces (varcas); with the stones of jambū and āmra, sour dadhittha and bilva, it is considered binding (sāṃgrāhika).
notes: Two gruels. The compound in line b can also be divided "stones of jambū and āmra, dadhittha, a sour (ingredient) and bilva". Identifications: māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo, Hindi उड़द (standard); jambū = Syzygium cumini, Hindi जामुन (standard); āmra = mango, Mangifera indica, Hindi आम (standard).

words.gloss: with alkali (kṣāra), citraka, hiṅgu and amlavetasa

hindi: क्षार, चित्रक, हिङ्गु और अम्लवेतस से यह भेदिनी मानी गई है; अभया, पिप्पलीमूल और विश्वा से वातानुलोमनी।
english: With alkali (kṣāra), citraka, hiṅgu and amlavetasa it is considered breaking (bhedin); with abhayā, pippalīmūla and viśvā, it moves Vāta downward (vātānulomana).
notes: Two gruels. bhedin: breaking up hard faeces, purgative. Identifications: hiṅgu = asafoetida, Ferula assa-foetida, Hindi हींग (standard); amlavetasa = disputed (Garcinia pedunculata and Rheum species proposed); abhayā = harītakī, Terminalia chebula, Hindi हरड़ (standard); viśvā = dry ginger, Hindi सोंठ (standard).

words.gloss: destroying the ill effects of ghee
in the ill effects of oil

hindi: तक्र में सिद्ध यवागू घृत की व्यापत्ति को नष्ट करती है; तैल की व्यापत्ति में तक्र और पिण्याक से सिद्ध यवागू प्रशस्त है।
english: Gruel cooked in buttermilk (takra) destroys the ill effects of ghee (ghṛta-vyāpatti); in the ill effects of oil, that prepared with buttermilk and oil-cake (piṇyāka) is recommended.
notes: Two gruels. vyāpatti/vyāpad: complications from taking ghee or oil wrongly, e.g. during oleation (commentators). piṇyāka = the cake left after pressing oil seeds.

hindi: गव्य मांसरस से, अम्ल सहित यवागू विषमज्वर को नष्ट करती है; यमक में पिप्पली और आमलक से पकाई गई यव की यवागू कण्ठ्य है।
english: With meat-juice (māṃsarasa) of cattle, soured, it destroys irregular fever (viṣamajvara); that of yava in yamaka, boiled with pippalī and āmalaka, is good for the throat.
notes: Two gruels. gavya = of cattle, bovine. viṣamajvara: irregular or intermittent fever; often equated with malaria-type fevers (probable). yamaka: see 27.

words.gloss: removing pain of the passage of semen

hindi: ताम्रचूड के रस में सिद्ध यवागू रेतोमार्ग की पीड़ा को दूर करती है; माष की दाल सहित, घृत और क्षीर से सिद्ध यवागू वृष्य है।
english: Cooked in the meat-juice of the cock (tāmracūḍa), it removes pain of the passage of semen; with split māṣa, prepared with ghee and milk, it is aphrodisiac (vṛṣya).
notes: Two gruels. tāmracūḍa, literally "copper-crested", is an ordinary word for the cock. rasa here is meat-juice, soup. vidala = split pulse.

words.gloss: with apāmārga, milk and godhā juice

hindi: उपोदिका और दधि से सिद्ध यवागू मद को नष्ट करती है; अपामार्ग, क्षीर और गोधा के रस से पकाई गई यवागू क्षुधा को नष्ट करती है।
english: Cooked with upodikā and curd (dadhi), it destroys intoxication (mada); boiled with apāmārga, milk and the meat-juice of godhā, it destroys hunger.
notes: Two gruels (the 27th and 28th). The compound in line b may also be divided "apāmārga-milk (milk with apāmārga) and godhā juice". godhā = monitor lizard (standard). Identification: upodikā = Malabar spinach, Basella alba, Hindi पोई (standard).

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक है: इस प्रकार ये अट्ठाईस यवागुएँ कही गई हैं, और पञ्चकर्मों को आधार बनाकर औषधियों का संग्रह कहा गया है।
english: Here is a verse: Thus these twenty-eight gruels have been proclaimed, and a collection of medicines has been declared on the basis of the five procedures (pañcakarma).

text_flags.why: Possible: the summary that follows has three verses (34 to 36), and the usual formula for several verses is 'tatra ślokāḥ' (as in chapter 1, 136). The singular may also be the edition's reading; not changed.

notes: 'tatra ślokaḥ' is the lead-in to the closing summary, kept as line a as the edition groups it; the summary runs to 36. The count is correct: units 18 to 33 give 28 gruels (18: one; 19 to 33: two each, 19 counting the gruel of 19a and the peyā of 19b).

words.gloss: for the sake of knowing roots and fruits
for the sake of knowledge based on the five procedures

hindi: जो औषध पहले मूल और फल के ज्ञान के हेतु कहा गया था, वह पञ्चकर्म पर आश्रित ज्ञान के हेतु फिर से कहा गया है।
english: The medicine that was stated earlier for the sake of knowing roots and fruits has been proclaimed again for the sake of knowledge based on the five procedures (pañcakarma).
notes: pūrvam probably refers to the lists of root-drugs and fruit-drugs in chapter 1 (mūlinī, phalinī). hetoḥ with the genitive: "for the sake of".

hindi: स्मृतिमान्, हेतु और युक्ति को जानने वाला, जितात्मा और प्रतिपत्तिमान् भिषक् औषधियों के संयोगों से चिकित्सा करने के योग्य होता है।
english: The physician who has memory, knows causes and rational planning (hetu, yukti), is self-controlled and has presence of mind, is fit to carry out treatment with combinations of medicines.

text_flags.why: The sense requires -jña (knower), as yuktijño in 16b; the Devanagari also has -जो (हेतुयुक्तिजो) without ञ. Typo.

notes: hetuyukti may also be one notion, "reasoning". pratipatti: presence of mind, readiness of understanding.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में अपामार्गतण्डुलीय नामक दूसरा अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Ślokasthāna of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the second chapter, named Apāmārgataṇḍulīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless. Ślokasthāna is another name of the Sūtrasthāna (chapter 1's colophon has sūtrasthāne); not flagged.
